notes: v1.14.568 — THE SERVER'S OWN WORDS REACH THE SCREEN. PUNCHLIST P-1, second half. One visible change: HTTP 400 joins phantomAPI's diagnostic classifier, so the response body is read and appended as '· server: <body>' exactly the way 401, 402, 403, 500, 502 and 503 already do. ⛔ WHY IT WAS NEEDED: 400 was the ONE error status the classifier did not handle, so it fell through to `return resp` and every caller rendered a bare code — vaAsk (:50964) turned it into 'API 400' and a technician in an aisle saw a number while the server's explanation sat unread in the body. ⭐ THIS SHIP IS REQUIRED REGARDLESS OF WHAT THE CLOUDFLARE LOG SAYS, per the owner: P-1 asks for the real error on screen, not a code. ⛔ A TRAP THAT WOULD HAVE TURNED A READABLE ERROR INTO A CRASH: the line `if (diag && friendly.indexOf(diag) === -1)` runs unconditionally, so adding 400 to the status guard WITHOUT giving it a branch in the friendly chain would leave `friendly` undefined and throw a TypeError on .indexOf. Both halves shipped together and the guard comment now records why they cannot be separated. ⚠ THE FRIENDLY TEXT IS DELIBERATELY THIN — Contract B10. The server's own words are the payload; a longer message would be inventing a diagnosis for an error nobody has read. An EMPTY body says so explicitly rather than showing a bare code with nothing after it, because 'the server rejected this and told us nothing' is itself the finding. ⚠ TWO BEHAVIOUR CHANGES, BOTH INTENDED: a 400 now raises a phantomToast the way the other classified statuses do, and phantomAPI now THROWS on 400 instead of returning the response — so edp_parseSection's own `throw new Error('HTTP ' + resp.status)` at :47817 is unreachable for 400 and its error text improves from 'HTTP 400' to the server's actual message. Both callers already funnel into a catch, so no path is left unhandled. ⚠ The body is still sliced to 200 characters for non-JSON responses, unchanged from the existing behaviour; JSON bodies surface error.message in full.
